mild.description: Absolute skewness above which a column is reported.

moderate.description: Absolute skewness above which the finding is a warning.

heavy.description: Absolute skewness above which the skew is called heavy.

gap_notice.description: Distance between the mean and the median, in standard deviations, from which the gap is reported. A long tail alone puts them up to about a third apart (an exponential, 0.31); a mix of two groups or a column that is mostly zero goes beyond that.

gap_warn.description: Gap, in standard deviations, from which the finding is a warning. The two can be at most 1 apart; a column that is 55% zero and exponential beyond that has a gap of 0.55, and one that is 70% zero 0.42.

gap_min_variance.description: Variance at or below which the gap is not reported: a column that barely varies is `near_zero_variance`'s to report.

skewness.description: Bias-corrected sample skewness; None when undefined, as for a constant column or fewer than three values.

level.description: How far the skewness is from zero; None when it is undefined.

gap_in_std.description: |mean − median| in standard deviations; None without a spread.

columns.description: Every numeric column with summary statistics, by name.
